transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Li (Redwood CSM), Jared Lawson (Orion Lead ML), Priya Kapoor (Orion Platform), Emily Park (Orion Security), Tariq Ahmed (Orion SRE)

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin, i'm sophie chen with redwood, mateo is our solutions engineer who will take most of the demo, ava from customer success is here for handoff. over to orion folks to intro?
[00:18] Jared: Jared here — lead on the ml infra side. we run inference on gcp right now, mixing hosted and a few in-house endpoints for compliance reasons. main ask is better observability for production issues — we get intermittent latency spikes and opaque errors.
[00:33] Priya: platform manager, interested in how we'd integrate logs into our splunk stack and RBAC for team-level access.
[00:40] Emily: security, want to confirm audit logs, retention, and KMS integration.
[00:46] Sophie: perfect. quick agenda: mateo will show the console tracing and request-logs flows, then we'll walk through a couple of debugging scenarios — slow p95, 500s, model fallback. then q&a and next steps.
[01:05] Mateo: alright i'll share my screen. so here's the Redwood console, main tracing dashboard. at the top you see an overview: requests per minute, median latency, p95/p99, error rate. we also surface pipeline-level traces — model load, token generation, kv-cache hit rates, and networking.
[01:33] [screen shows trace waterfall]
[01:36] Mateo: this is a single request trace. you can expand spans — you'll see 'router -> runtime -> model-infer -> kvcache lookup -> token generation' spans. a common cause of spikes we see is repeated cold model loads when variants aren't pinned, or large batch sizes mixing short and long sequences.
[01:57] Jared: can you show how we correlate trace ids with our app logs? we need to pull complete context into splunk.
[02:05] Mateo: yes — each request has a trace_id and we include request_id headers in the response. you can export request logs as JSON/CSV or ship them to your SIEM via our webhook connector. here's an example export; it includes prompt metadata, tokens generated, latency breakdowns, error codes.
[02:28] Priya: retention on those exports? we usually keep 90 days in our splunk.
[02:33] Mateo: console retains request-level logs for 30 days by default in hosted; for Dedicated or Private you can configure retention and direct S3 export to meet longer retention. audit logs are separate — we keep a tamper-evident audit trail for auth events and config changes.
[02:51] Emily: about encryption — data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys?
[02:55] Sophie: yes with Private deployments you can integrate KMS/HSM and opt to manage keys. Hosted can be configured with BYOK for enterprise plans.
[03:06] Tariq: can we attach our SSO? we need SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[03:10] Mateo: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM is supported, plus RBAC roles that map to console permissions — you can restrict access to traces and exports.
[03:20] Mateo: going back to the trace, i'll flip to the error-analysis view. you can filter by error code, model, route, and look at aggregated error clusters. for example, here we have a cluster of 'runtime:kv-miss' that correlates with longer generation times.
[03:38] Mateo: we also surface anomalous output — if a client-defined eval metric drops, the console flags it and shows diffs across model versions. this helps triage whether it's a model regression or prompt change.
[03:51] Jared: nice. how do rollbacks and automatic fallbacks work? we want graceful degradation if the main model is down.
[03:58] Mateo: you can define rollout policies per route: primary model, fallback model(s), region fallback, and capacity tiers. on failures we automatically route to the next compatible variant. traces show fallback events so you can count how often fallback occurred.
[04:18] Priya: show the request-logs CSV sample please, mateo.
[04:22] Mateo: sure — exporting is two clicks. here's the CSV preview: timestamp, request_id, trace_id, route, model, prompt_size, generated_tokens, total_latency_ms, infra_latency_ms, model_latency_ms, error_code, error_message. you can query in console or push to S3.
[04:44] Emily: are error messages pseudonymized? we don't want full PHI/PII in logs when requests include customer data.
[04:50] Sophie: good call — we have configurable redaction rules and PII scrubbing on exports. for compliance-sensitive customers we recommend Private deployment and in-line scrubbing rules before logs leave the VPC.
[05:06] Mateo: next scenario — debugging a slow p95. here i filter to a timeframe with p95 spike. console shows a heatmap by route and a trace sample with stacked spans. you can see model_latency jumped due to a cold-start during a burst; kv-cache miss rate was high on that route.
[05:25] Mateo: we surface suggested actions — enable prefix caching for that route, increase warm pool, or pin model variant to avoid cold loads. we also highlight batch-size mismatches; if your clients send single-token requests, batching might hurt tail latency.
[05:41] Jared: we do a mix of short completions for UI and longer async jobs. how granular are batching controls? can we set per-route batching thresholds?
[05:50] Mateo: yes, batching and batching windows are per-route. you can also set cost/latency profiles that bias toward lower cost (bigger batches) or lower latency (smaller batches). we show estimated cost delta in the console heuristics.
[06:06] Priya: what about request sampling? we can't export every query at high volume.
[06:10] Mateo: sampling controls exist — head-based sampling, error-only sampling, and adaptive sampling where more anomalous flows are retained at higher rates. you can also instrument your SDK to forward only flagged requests.
[06:22] Mateo: now i want to demo a 500-level error. expanding the error cluster, here's the stack: runtime timed out communicating with model-backend, error code 504. the trace shows network retry loops. console surfaces the top affected routes and frequency, plus the original payload for debug (if retention allows).
[06:46] Emily: do we get retry metadata? we need to see how many retries and backoff.
[06:50] Mateo: yes, each span contains retry_count and backoff_ms. we also surface per-request header capture so you can correlate client retry loops.
[06:59] Jared: when you say "original payload" is that the full prompt? again that raises PII concerns.
[07:03] Mateo: by default we mask or redact fields flagged as PII; full payload retention is configurable and typically restricted for enterprise plans with appropriate data processing addenda.
[07:16] Sophie: for your environment, we'd recommend Private deployment but we can also run a Dedicated pilot with S3 exports and BYOK if you prefer hosted control plane with network isolation.
[07:27] Tariq: what about on-prem? we have some air-gapped requirements for certain customers.
[07:30] Mateo: we support on-prem packages — shipping the runtime and console connectors into an air-gapped environment, with local control plane. support model updates via signed bundles.
[07:42] Jared: curious about tracing overhead — adding spans can add latency. what's the instrumentation cost?
[07:47] Mateo: tracing is lightweight; spans are emitted asynchronously and sampling keeps overhead minimal. we measured <1% median latency overhead in our benchmarks with default sampling. full trace capture is optional per-route.
[08:01] Priya: can we programmatically query the console APIs to fetch traces for alarms?
[08:05] Mateo: yes, there's a traces API and request-logs API. you can pull JSON and integrate with alerting systems. we also have built-in alerting that triggers on p95, error-rate, or anomalous model degradations.
[08:17] [demo continues, Mateo toggles to request log query]
[08:18] Mateo: here's a saved query that finds all requests with model_latency_ms > 2000 and error_code != null. you can save queries and attach to alerts or have them export to S3 automatically.
[08:30] Jared: how long does it take to spin up a canary route and test a model variant?
[08:34] Mateo: you can deploy a canary in minutes; console supports traffic splits (e.g., 1%) and will show per-variant metrics so you can detect regressions early.
[08:44] Emily: audit trail question again — if someone rotates a key or changes a rollout, do we have an immutable log?
[08:50] Sophie: yes, we show config changes with actor, timestamp, before/after and you can forward audit logs to your SIEM. for Private we can sign the logs and store them in a customer-owned S3 bucket.
[09:03] Mateo: last quick thing — the error-analysis view links directly to the raw request log and the trace. you can jump from aggregated error cluster straight to X sample traces so debugging is fast.
[09:16] Jared: in terms of triage, can we add annotations? our SREs like to leave notes on incidents.
[09:20] Mateo: annotation support is there; notes are part of the trace metadata and are searchable. you can restrict note creation to certain roles.
[09:27] Priya: any built-in dashboards for business metrics? we want to tie cost per request to user features.
[09:32] Mateo: yes per-route cost breakdowns, token-level billing, and you can attach tags to routes for product metrics. cost estimation for changes (e.g., enabling caching or quantizing) is surfaced in recommendations.
[09:46] [brief lag while screen-share changes]
[09:55] Sophie: open to questions — anything we didn't cover?
[09:58] Emily: what is the SLA for Dedicated?
[10:01] Sophie: Dedicated has an SLA for uptime and p99 latency targets — the numbers are in the pricing/enterprise docs i'll send. typically 99.9%+ with contractual penalties.
[10:12] Jared: let's talk practical pilot scope — we'd like to test 3 routes: ui-completions (low-latency), billing-batch (high-throughput), and fraud-check (sensitive data). can you support separate retention and scrubbing policies per route?
[10:29] Mateo: yes, route-level retention and scrubbing are supported. for fraud-check i'd recommend Private or Dedicated with BYOK and stricter retention rules.
[10:39] Sophie: great — recap of next steps then. sophie will send pricing and security docs, mateo will export sample request logs and tracing screenshots, jared will share 3 example prompts and p95 targets, and we will schedule a pilot kickoff.
[10:56] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:00] Sophie: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with dates.

[end of transcript]
